Fanatic

fuh-NAT-ik -- stress on the second syllable, NAT. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fanatic is a person filled with excessive passion or enthusiasm.

A lifelong fanatic about chess, Grandpa carries a folding board everywhere he goes, just in case.

Worked Example

One neighbor repaints his entire den in his team's colors, drives nine hours to away games, and names his three goldfish after the starting midfielders.

Passion that intense -- far beyond ordinary enthusiasm -- is what makes him a fanatic. The word is a noun for a person whose devotion to something has grown excessive, even a little alarming.

How Fanatic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

zealot

zealot: a person with extreme, uncompromising devotion

enthusiast

enthusiast: a person with a lively, eager interest

devotee

devotee: a person strongly dedicated to something

Antonyms

skeptic

skeptic: a person who doubts and questions claims

moderate

moderate: a person with restrained, balanced views

How Strong Is It? — enthusiast → zealot → fanatic

enthusiast vs. fanatic

enthusiast vs. fanatic: Enthusiast is warmer and far milder than fanatic -- an enthusiast loves their hobby in a healthy way, while a fanatic's passion has tipped over into excess that crowds out everything else.

zealot vs. fanatic

zealot vs. fanatic: Zealot pushes past even fanatic: a fanatic's devotion is excessive, but a zealot's is extreme and uncompromising, often demanding that everyone else share it too.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — fanat-

root — fanat-: of a temple; frenzied, as if inspired by a temple deity (Latin fanaticus, from fanum 'temple')

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Fanatic goes back to Latin fanum, 'temple.' A fanaticus was someone in a wild frenzy, as if possessed by a temple's deity. Today's fanatic keeps that image: a person whose passion for something burns with an almost religious, out-of-control intensity.

Use the root in a new word: profane

Use the root in a new word: profane: The knights considered it profane to carry weapons into the shrine.

Root Check

Word Choice

Fun fact: the everyday word 'fan' -- as in a sports fan -- is not a separate word at all; it is a nineteenth-century shortening of fanatic. Remember that fanatic is a noun for a person: he is 'a fanatic about model trains.' The matching adjective is 'fanatical' -- fanatical devotion, never 'a fanatic devotion.'
